subtitle: How a poet’s village songs crossed oceans and returned as a school under the sky

panels.shot: epic medium-wide of Tagore seated under a banyan in Santiniketan, manuscripts in hand, faint silhouettes of ships and a snowy European cityscape rising behind him like clouds
panels.action: Rabindranath Tagore sits cross-legged beneath a spreading tree at Santiniketan, holding loose pages of verse, as ghostly outlines of a steamship and a distant European city glow above the horizon.

dialogue.text: From songs born in a quiet Bengal courtyard to the Nobel in distant Stockholm, how did Rabindranath Tagore turn world fame into a school beneath the open sky?

i18n.hi: शांत बंगाली आँगन से जन्मे गीत स्टॉकहोम के नोबेल तक, रवीन्द्रनाथ ने दुनिया की शोहरत को खुले आसमान की पाठशाला में कैसे बदला?

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of Jorasanko mansion, lamplit, with Tagore at a desk surrounded by Bengali manuscripts
panels.action: Rabindranath Tagore, bearded and absorbed, leans over a cluttered desk in the Jorasanko home, Bengali manuscripts spread around him as a single oil lamp throws warm light and deep shadows.

dialogue.text: Calcutta, 1910. In the Jorasanko house, Rabindranath gathers years of verse into a single Bengali volume he calls Gitanjali, song-offerings for an unseen listener.

i18n.hi: कलकत्ता, 1910। जोरासांको के घर में, रवीन्द्रनाथ अपने बरसों के गीतों को एक ही बंगाली किताब में समेटते हैं—गीतांजलि, अनदेखे श्रोता के लिए गीत-अर्पण।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Tagore’s hand writing with a pen, Bengali lines on one side, English prose on another notebook
panels.action: Tagore’s weathered hand moves between two notebooks on a low table, one filled with flowing Bengali script, the other with careful English prose, as he pauses often, eyes distant.

dialogue.text: Two years later, on the voyage to England and in quiet stops, he reshapes these songs into English prose, not line by line, but as fresh offerings in another tongue.

i18n.hi: दो साल बाद, इंग्लैंड की समुद्री यात्रा में और शांत ठहरावों पर, वे इन्हें अंग्रेज़ी गद्य में ढालते हैं—शब्दशः नहीं, जैसे दूसरी ज़ुबान में नए अर्पण।

panels.shot: medium shot in a small London drawing room, Tagore reading softly as a small mixed group of British listeners lean forward
panels.action: In a modest London drawing room, Tagore sits simply dressed, reading from his English Gitanjali while a circle of attentive British men and women listen, some eyes closed, the coal fire glowing behind.

dialogue.text: In London parlours, he reads these prose songs aloud. The English is simple, almost bare, yet in the still rooms, listeners hear something new and very old at once.

i18n.hi: लंदन के ड्रॉइंगरूमों में वे ये गद्य-गीत ज़ोर से पढ़ते हैं। अंग्रेज़ी सीधी, लगभग नंगी; फिर भी सन्नाटे में लोग एक साथ कुछ नया और बहुत पुराना सुनते हैं।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of a British poet (un-cast silhouette) holding the Gitanjali manuscript with scribbled preface notes, Tagore in soft focus beyond
panels.action: A British poet, seen only from behind, holds the worn Gitanjali manuscript, margins crowded with admiring notes, as Tagore sits by the window, framed in London fog.

dialogue.text: Friends and poets in England carry his manuscript to a publisher. Their prefaces and praise open doors his own quiet voice might not have reached alone.

i18n.hi: इंग्लैंड के दोस्त और कवि पांडुलिपि लेकर प्रकाशक तक जाते हैं। उनकी भूमिका और तारीफ़ ऐसे दरवाज़े खोलती है जहाँ रवीन्द्रनाथ की धीमी आवाज़ अकेले न पहुँच पाती।

panels.shot: graphic close-up of the title page of Gitanjali: Song Offerings being opened by Tagore, his face reflected faintly in the glass of a window
panels.action: Tagore gently opens a fresh copy of Gitanjali: Song Offerings, the crisp English title page catching the light while his thoughtful face appears faintly mirrored in the adjacent windowpane.

dialogue.text: In 1912, Gitanjali: Song Offerings appears in London, one hundred and three pieces of prose, drawn from the Bengali volume yet altered, pruned, merged, as if rewritten for another ear.

i18n.hi: 1912 में ‘Gitanjali: Song Offerings’ लंदन में छपती है—सौ तीन गद्य-रचनाएँ, बंगाली गीतांजलि से ली हुई, पर काट-छाँट, मेल-मिलाप के साथ, जैसे किसी और कान के लिए फिर से लिखी गई हों।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye of a map from Calcutta to London to Stockholm, with Tagore’s small figure walking along an ink-drawn line
panels.action: On an old-style map stretching from Calcutta to London and up to Stockholm, a tiny figure of Tagore walks along a dark ink line that winds through sea and land.

dialogue.text: The prose poems travel further than he does. In Stockholm, academicians read them in English and translation, arguing over their strangeness and their clarity.

i18n.hi: ये गद्य-कविताएँ उससे आगे निकल जाती हैं। स्टॉकहोम में अकादमिक इन्हें अंग्रेज़ी और अनुवाद में पढ़ते हैं, उनकी अनोखापन और साफ़गोई पर बहस करते हैं।

panels.shot: medium-wide of Tagore in Santiniketan receiving a telegram, students and trees around him
panels.action: Under the sparse shade of Santiniketan’s trees, Tagore stands among barefoot students as a messenger hands him a telegram; curious faces look on while the dry earth stretches beyond.

dialogue.text: On 13 November 1913, a telegram reaches Santiniketan. Rabindranath Tagore is named the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature, honoured for his deeply sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse.

i18n.hi: 13 नवंबर 1913 को एक तार शांति निकेतन पहुँचता है। रवीन्द्रनाथ ठाकुर साहित्य में पहले गैर-यूरोपीय नोबेल विजेता घोषित होते हैं, उनके गहरे संवेदनशील, ताज़ा और सुंदर काव्य के लिए।

panels.shot: close-up on Tagore’s face as he reads the telegram, a mix of surprise and inwardness
panels.action: Tagore holds the thin slip of paper close, his brows slightly raised, lips pressed, eyes reflecting neither triumph nor disbelief but a quiet inward turning.

dialogue.speaker: rabindranath_tagore
dialogue.text: This honour belongs first to the songs, and to the land that shaped them.

i18n.hi: ये मान पहले उन्हीं गीतों का है, और उस धरती का जिसने उन्हें जन्म दिया।

panels.shot: formal medium shot of Tagore at a modest ceremony in India, being addressed as Nobel laureate, British officials present
panels.action: In a genteel hall in India, Tagore sits in plain robes as British officials and Indian leaders in coats and turbans look toward him, some applauding, a small medal case resting on a table.

dialogue.text: In cities and courts he is celebrated, knighted by the British Crown soon after. Yet he returns again and again to Santiniketan, seeing the Nobel not as an arrival, but as a resource.

i18n.hi: शहरों और दरबारों में उनका स्वागत होता है, जल्द ही ब्रितानी साम्राज्य से ‘नाइटहुड’ भी मिलता है। फिर भी वे बार-बार शांति निकेतन लौटते हैं, नोबेल को मंज़िल नहीं, एक साधन मानकर।

panels.shot: wide pastoral shot of Santiniketan classes under trees, Tagore walking among children
panels.action: On the open fields of Santiniketan, children sit in loose circles beneath trees, slate and book in hand, while Tagore walks slowly among them, robe stirring in the light dust, sky vast overhead.

dialogue.text: He pours royalties and gifts into this experiment in learning under the sky, shaping Santiniketan into Visva-Bharati, a world-university rooted in village soil.

i18n.hi: वे रॉयल्टी और उपहारों को खुले आसमान की इस पाठशाला में उड़ेल देते हैं, शांति निकेतन को विश्व-भारती में ढालते हैं—गाँव की मिट्टी में जड़ें जमाए विश्वविद्यालाय।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tagore speaking with a small group of Indian and foreign teachers under a verandah
panels.action: Tagore stands beneath a simple verandah, gesturing gently as Indian and foreign teachers listen, some with notebooks, the fields and an unfinished brick building visible beyond.

dialogue.speaker: rabindranath_tagore
dialogue.text: Let the cultures of the world meet here, without walls between child and earth.

i18n.hi: दुनिया की तमाम संस्कृतियाँ यहाँ मिलें—बिना दीवारों के, बच्चे और धरती के बीच।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Tagore alone at a desk at night, newspapers about world war and nationalism scattered, a manuscript of Ghare Baire nearby
panels.action: Late at night, Tagore sits by a dim lamp, newspapers on war and rallies spread beside a manuscript of Ghare Baire, his face lined with concern as distant drums of politics are imagined beyond the walls.

dialogue.text: As fame grows, he writes against aggressive nationalism, warning in essays and in Ghare Baire of the dangers when love of country hardens into worship of the collective self.

i18n.hi: यश बढ़ते ही वे उग्र राष्ट्रवाद के विरुद्ध लिखते हैं, निबंधों में और ‘घरे-बाहरे’ में चेतावनी देते हैं कि देशप्रेम जब सामूहिक अहंकार की पूजा बन जाए, तो वह खतरनाक है।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Tagore reading a report of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, light falling starkly on the page
panels.action: Tagore sits stiffly upright, a letter or newspaper in his hands describing the killings at Jallianwala Bagh; the light strikes the page harshly while the rest of the room falls into shadow.

dialogue.text: In 1919, news from Amritsar reaches him: unarmed men, women and children fired upon in Jallianwala Bagh. His protest must now speak not in verse, but in a public act.

i18n.hi: 1919 में अमृतसर से खबर आती है—जलियाँवाला बाग़ में निहत्थे औरतों, बच्चों, मर्दों पर गोलियाँ चलीं। अब उसका विरोध कविता से नहीं, खुले सार्वजनिक कदम से बोलेगा।

panels.shot: close-up of Tagore’s hand writing the letter returning his knighthood, the discarded knighthood insignia lying to one side
panels.action: On a plain table, Tagore’s hand moves steadily across a sheet, composing the letter that returns his knighthood, while the small insignia lies set aside, its ribbon coiled and unused.

dialogue.text: He writes to the Viceroy, giving up the title of ‘Sir’, declaring he cannot accept honours from a government that has, in his words, stained its name with wanton cruelty.

i18n.hi: वे वायसराय को लिखते हैं, ‘सर’ की उपाधि लौटाते हुए कहते हैं, वे ऐसे शासन का सम्मान नहीं रख सकते जिसने, उनके शब्दों में, अपने नाम पर बेमानी क्रूरता का धब्बा लगा लिया हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tagore addressing a small gathering at Santiniketan after sending the letter, students and colleagues listening
panels.action: In the courtyard at Santiniketan, Tagore stands before a small gathering of students and colleagues, posture composed yet firm, as they listen in silence to his explanation of the renounced honour.

dialogue.speaker: rabindranath_tagore
dialogue.text: An honour can be set aside; a conscience, once silenced, cannot be recovered.

i18n.hi: सम्मान छोड़ा जा सकता है; पर जो अंतःकरण एक बार दबा दिया जाए, उसे फिर जिंदा नहीं किया जा सकता।

panels.shot: gentle wide shot of Tagore walking with children at Santiniketan at dusk, Visva-Bharati buildings taking shape in the background
panels.action: At dusk, Tagore walks slowly with a line of children along a dusty path, as simple halls and structures of Visva-Bharati rise in the background against a softening sky.

dialogue.text: Through awards, protests, praise and criticism, he returns to the same work: weaving song, school and world together, so that learning in this corner of Bengal may belong to all humankind.

i18n.hi: पुरस्कारों, विरोध, प्रशंसा और आलोचना के बीच, वे उसी काम पर लौटते हैं—गीत, पाठशाला और दुनिया को बुनना, ताकि बंगाल के इस कोने की शिक्षा पूरी मानवता की हो सके।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of Tagore under a tree, eyes half-closed, children playing in the distance, faint outlines of distant cities in the sky
panels.action: Tagore sits once more beneath a tree, eyes half-closed in thought, while children play in the distance and the faint shapes of faraway cities shimmer high above the horizon like distant clouds.

dialogue.text: Rooted in Bengali song yet heard in many tongues, his Gitanjali and Visva-Bharati ask still: can a voice stay true to its own soil and yet offer its song freely to the world?

i18n.hi: बंगाली गीत में जड़ें, पर कई ज़ुबानों में गूँजती—उनकी ‘गीतांजलि’ और ‘विश्व-भारती’ अब भी पूछती हैं: क्या कोई आवाज़ अपनी मिट्टी सच्चाई से थामे रखकर भी अपना गीत दुनिया को खुला दे सकती है?

subtitle_i18n.en: How a poet’s village songs crossed oceans and returned as a school under the sky
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक कवि के गाँव के गीत समंदर पार गए और लौटकर खुले आकाश का पाठशाला बन गए
